$comment: The two classification axes hatsu:classify applies to an issue or an inline effort (the maintainer's rulings of 2026-10-04, docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-04 -- classify and direct). Axis one is the programming LANGUAGE the work needs; axis two is the JOB -- a compact, domain-agnostic vocabulary that folds the 114 phase keys of the source document (Version-Decoupled Model Selection Matrix for Engineering Workflows, registry snapshot 2026-10-04) into 39 jobs, each carrying the document phases it stands for per domain, the FIRST listed being the phase hatsu:direct routes on. The five domains (feature, maintenance, parity, aigov, library) are DERIVED, never labelled: `domains.rule` says how. Labels are `<prefix><key>` with no namespace (ruling: lang/<key> + job/<key>); nen reads each axis structurally as one family through its prefix and hard-codes none of these names -- this file is data a consumer's nen/labels.json is populated from through `nen classify install`, and labels.json stays the one source of truth for the repository's labels (the install lands through a declaration PR first, GitHub is synced after). Companion formats (YAML, JSON, XML, CSS, shell, PowerShell, Markdown...) are never labelled: they ride the language they serve. An axis the classifier cannot decide with confidence stays EMPTY and the issue is listed as undecidable (nen's own `undecidable` discipline), never a best guess. Read by hatsu:classify, hatsu:file, hatsu:direct and nen's `classify` family (--taxonomy <this path>).

rule.when: nen repo classify reports kind process, or role canon
nen repo classify reports kind library
the issue carries the repository's bug kind label (a label named bug, or <ns>:bug), or every job it carries lists only maintenance phases

domains.fallback: A job with no phase in the derived domain routes on the first domain it does list, in this order: the derived domain, maintenance, feature, library, aigov, parity. The report names the substitution.
domains.$comment: The domain is a run-time derivation from the repository's kind (nen repo classify) and the issue's own kind label, never a label of its own: a product repository's bug is maintenance work, its enhancement feature work; a process repository is always aigov; a library always library; job/parity is the one marker that moves a product issue into the parity table.

confidence.$comment: A sweep applies high- and medium-confidence rows after its one confirmation; low-confidence rows are listed separately and skipped unless picked. An axis with no confident answer stays empty: the issue is listed as undecidable with the reason, and a re-run picks it up again.

lang: file paths and extensions named in the issue
frameworks and toolchains named (SwiftUI, Compose, React, WinUI, Gradle, Xcode...)
the repository's declared lane stacks (nen/contract.json project.lanes[].stack)
the repository's kind: a process repository's governance work is prose
job: the issue's kind label (bug -> triage or bug-fix first)
verbs in the title and acceptance criteria (design, implement, test, release, migrate, document...)
the paths it names (skills and agents -> prose-authoring; contracts/ and nen/*.json -> schema; surfaces/ -> adapters; .github/workflows -> ci-cd)
the parity vocabulary (port, parity, cross-platform, same as on <platform>)
